text:
maria: ran an overnight sweep comparing flash_fused, flash_paged, and flash_v2 on a100-1. noticed weird cost delta when KV cache is hot

devon: how weird? numbers?

maria: short summary: with KV=true and steady traffic we expected paged to win for long-context sessions, but flash_fused throughput dropped vs flash_paged for our 2k-seq KV workload. quick dump: 
```
kernel=flash_fused  batch=4 seq=2048 kv=true  tokens/sec=2120  tokens/hr=7,632,000  gpu_cost_hr=$2.5  $/M_tokens=0.327
kernel=flash_paged   batch=4 seq=2048 kv=true  tokens/sec=2610  tokens/hr=9,396,000  $/M_tokens=0.266
kernel=flash_v2      batch=4 seq=2048 kv=true  tokens/sec=2400  tokens/hr=8,640,000  $/M_tokens=0.289
```
maria: that 22% throughput delta between fused and paged becomes ~23% higher $/M for fused -> not just latency, it's unit-econ regression on high-KV sessions

devon: what was the batching heuristic? were we coalescing single-session requests differently?

maria: rollout used heuristic "steady-state-batch" that picks target_batch=8 for short tails, but for these KV-hot flows most requests are 1-2 items and we leave them single-session; runner falls back to smaller micro-batches due to seq variability

ricardo: do we have profiler traces? nvprof/nsys or kernel-level counters?
maria: yes attached a short flame dump from nsight (trimmed):
```
# fused (slow path)
cat kernel_times.txt | grep Attn | head
attn_forward  elapsed_ms=18.4  calls=5200
kv_pack      elapsed_ms=4.2   calls=5200
memcpy_htod  elapsed_ms=3.8

# paged (fast path)
attn_forward  elapsed_ms=13.2  calls=5200
kv_pack      elapsed_ms=2.1   calls=5200
memcpy_htod  elapsed_ms=2.9
```
maria: looks like fused variant triggers bigger attn kernel time and extra mem pressure when KV pages are touched frequently

anna: could be kernel selection logic picks fused when seq < threshold but misses kv-hit ratio. we should include KV hit metric in selector.

ricardo: agree. proposal: selector takes (seq, batch, kv_hit_rate, avg_seq) -> prefer paged if kv_hit_rate > 0.6 and seq > 512. quick A/B math: for our typical workloads that flips 45% of sessions to paged and reduces $/M by ~10% overall.

kira: ops question: safe to canary selector change? need rollback path if we hit tail-latency regression. can we do staged rollout by customer tier?
maria: yes, plan: canary 5% internal -> 5 customers -> 25% -> global. metrics to watch: tokens/sec, p99, GPU utilisation, and $/M tokens. perf-bot will synthesize tokens/sec and cost every 5m.

perf-bot: scheduled job created: "attention-selector-canary"  interval=5m metrics=[tokens/sec,p99,gpu_util,$/M_tokens] notify=#eng-runtime if delta > 5%

devon: one more ask — please record batching distribution (batch sizes over time). last time we missed a bug where the scheduler suppressed batching for sessions with KV due to sticky affinities.
maria: good call. i'll add histogram exports and a tiny agent metric: `kv_session_batch_ratio`

ricardo: also, run variant tests with different quantization profiles; fused sometimes performs worse with certain int8 kernels. add flash_v2_int8 into the sweep.

maria: will do. next steps: 1) change selector to include kv_hit_rate threshold, 2) add batching histogram, 3) canary rollout plan, 4) add flash_v2_int8 sweep. I'll post raw traces + perf-bot dashboards once done. :+1:

kira: thanks — please @devon when dashboards are live

maria: will do — tagging notes in the PR when it's up
